items.content_html:
Summary

Chrome 148 shipped the new HTML setters and streaming APIs behind a flag, and we're planning on releasing them unflagged from Chrome 154:
https://developer.chrome.com/blog/declarative-partial-updates#renewed_html_insertion_and_streaming_methods

I'd like to start adding them to BCD in prep for that, and also to kick off the web features PR.

At the moment I've marked most of them as "standard_track": false even though they are going through standardisation because we don't have spec links yet. Will update those when whatwg/html#12758 lands.

I've also corrected setHTMLUnsafe support of options.sanitizer which was included in Chrome 146 (tests showing this). Looks like this was updated incorrectly in #28302

Test results and supporting details

https://wpt.fyi/results/domparsing/tentative?label=experimental&label=master&aligned

https://chromestatus.com/feature/5054329641893888

Related issues

Summary

Add compatibility data for the RTCRtpEncodingParameters.scalabilityMode parameter used by WebRTC SVC.

The new data covers both API paths where the parameter can be provided:

  • RTCRtpSender.setParameters() via parameters.encodings
  • RTCPeerConnection.addTransceiver() via init.sendEncodings

Test results and supporting details

  • npm run format passed.
  • BCD linting passed with no errors.
  • The test suite passed: 338 tests passed, 0 failed.
  • git diff --check passed.
  • Chrome support is recorded from version 111 based on the WebRTC SVC implementation.
  • Firefox and Safari are recorded as unsupported for this specific encoding parameter.

Supporting specification:
https://w3c.github.io/webrtc-svc/#dom-rtcrtpencodingparameters-scalabilitymode

Related issues

Fixes #25720

The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.20.7) found new features shipping in Chromium 153 beta which was released yesterday. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Canary/behind flags, it is not considered here.

With this PR, BCD will consider the following features as shipping in Chromium 153 (bold features are new keys in BCD).

  • api.BaseAudioContext.renderQuantumSize (ref)
  • api.Document.browsingTopics (removal) (ref)
  • api.HTMLElement.autocorrect (152->153) (ref)
  • api.HTMLIFrameElement.browsingTopics (removal) (ref)
  • css.properties.scroll-axis-lock (ref)
  • css.properties.scroll-axis-lock.auto (ref)
  • css.properties.scroll-axis-lock.none (ref)
  • javascript.builtins.Iterator.join (ref)
  • javascript.builtins.Iterator.zip (ref)
  • javascript.builtins.Iterator.zipKeyed (ref)

See also https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-153-beta and https://chromestatus.com/roadmap

Note: There are also new capability elements: <camera> and <microphone>, however, they are not in a spec which is considered by browser-specs, see w3c/browser-specs#1915. I will follow-up on these separately.

items.content_html:
Fixes #29241

This PR adds a new compatibility entry documenting that writing-mode: vertical-* does not work on <th> or <td> elements on iOS Safari before version 17.

The current data shows safari_ios: "mirror" which incorrectly implies full support from iOS 9+. In reality, table cell elements only received support starting from iOS 17.

items.content_html:
Summary

Add compatibility data for the Firefox-only behavior of Selection.addRange() supporting multiple selection ranges.

The existing Selection.addRange() support data remains unchanged. This adds an adds_multiple_ranges subfeature indicating support in Firefox 51 and later, while marking the behavior as non-standard and unsupported in other browsers.

Test results and supporting details

  • npm run lint — passed with 0 errors.
  • npm run format — passed; Prettier reported all files correctly formatted and TypeScript produced no errors.
  • Full unit test suite — 315 tests passed, 0 failed.
  • git diff --check — passed.

The behavior is documented by the Selection API specification and is also reflected in the existing BCD precedent for Firefox-only multiple-range behavior in Selection.getComposedRanges().

Related issues

Fixes #28742
items.title: fix(api): document multiple ranges in Selection.addRange

This is a follow-up PR to #29823

The https://collector.openwebdocs.org project (v10.20.5) found new features shipping in Safari 27 beta (22625.1.24.11.2) on macOS 27.0 Beta (26A5388g).

ariaNotify (as found in the first run already) is now also officially mentioned as shipping:
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-release-notes/safari-27-release-notes

The deprecated maxInterStageShaderComponents has been removed.

The release notes also say "Added support for the TC39 BigInt Math proposal, exposing Math-equivalent methods on BigInt such as BigInt.pow and BigInt.sqrt. (152472996)" but I can't confirm this. I think it might be behind a (JSC) flag.

@jdatapple, can you review? Am I missing things for the new Safari 27 beta?
